supplies: A suitcase or bag from a trip
One of your dog's own toys
substitutes: No suitcase? A backpack, tote bag or pillowcase from a trip works.
No sign? Fold a sheet of paper into a tent.
title: The Suitcase Unpacking
clue: Something has just come home from far away, and it smells of everywhere.
reveal: Home from a trip, your dog unpacks the suitcase by nose. You clear the case of hazards, lay a few safe things on a towel, and tell the story of each smell while your dog investigates at their own pace.
objective: After a trip, set out a hazard-checked open case of travel smells and let your dog sniff through it while you tell the story of the journey.
instructions: Before you unpack anything, strip the case of hazards: medication, toiletries, snacks, gum, chocolate, coins, batteries, chargers, anything small or sharp. Check pockets and linings and put it all out of reach.

Pick three to five safe things from the trip: a worn scarf, a hotel towel, a folded worn T-shirt, a cardboard ticket sleeve too big to swallow, an empty bag. Cloth, leather and paper hold smells well.

Set up the Arrivals Hall: spread a towel in a quiet room, lay the open, empty case flat, and prop a paper sign reading ARRIVALS beside it. Unzip it before your dog comes in so the zip sound does not startle them.
The customs find: roll your dog's own toy inside one clean cloth and tuck it into the case.
Bring your dog in and sit down. No pointing. Let them sniff the case and each item for as long as they like. They may skip any or all.
Tell the story aloud as they go, quietly: 'That is the train. That is the hotel corridor.' Give each item one line.
If they find the toy, the customs find is theirs to keep. If not, lift a corner of the cloth to show it.
Finish by putting everything from the case away out of reach: nothing from it stays with your dog afterwards. Write the trip and your dog's most-sniffed item on a paper tag for yourself.
twist: Your dog gets the first look at your trip, and the smells tell its story: a homecoming that begins at the suitcase instead of the sofa.
variations: Quick: one scarf on the doorstep and a three-minute sniff.
Day-out edition: unpack the tote from a day trip with the same hazard check. No leftovers or food wrappers.
Nervous dog or puppy: skip the zip, keep the case open and quiet, offer one item and let them come to it.
Customs Desk: line up four open bags, one holding the toy, and see which one your dog's nose picks first.
completion: Your dog has sniffed the case or items at their own pace, or walked past while you told the story, and the trip tag is written.
photoIdea: Your dog's nose deep in the open case, shot from the side while they are absorbed. No posing.
memoryPrompt: Which smell held your dog's attention longest?
safety: Clear the case of medication, chocolate, gum, batteries and anything small or sharp, pockets included.
Skip strong scents like perfume or insect spray; they are much stronger to a dog's nose.
